# 破迷正道歌--鍾離權

**ID:** KR5a0282
**Custom ID:** ZB5a0282

## Authors / Editors
- 鍾離權

**Editions:** SJB, ZHDZ

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A short *nèidān* 內丹 poem in seven-character verse in one juan, preserved in the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* 正統道藏 (DZ 270 / CT 270 = TC 2:832–833), 洞真部 眾術類. The poem is attributed to the legendary Zhōnglí Quán 鍾離權 (Zhèngyáng zhēnrén 正陽真人), one of the two patriarchs of the **Zhōng Lǚ** 鍾呂 inner-alchemical lineage. Despite its attribution, the poem is not quoted in its present form in any earlier Sòng work; the earliest mention of a *Pòmí gēlùn* 破迷歌論 by Zhōnglí Quán is in *[Sānjí zhīmìng quántǐ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0275)* 15b (ca. 1250), but in the absence of a quotation it cannot be confirmed that the title there refers to the present poem. During the Yuán dynasty (1279–1368), a different poem also circulated under the title *Zhèngyáng wēng zhīmí gē* 正陽翁指迷歌 (cf. *[Shàngyáng zǐ jīndān dàyào](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d1067)* 9.6a), so multiple poems with similar titles were in circulation. There exist further variant versions even of the present poem (cf. 1b of the present text and *[Bǎoyī zǐ Sānfēng lǎorén dānjué](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0281)* 11b); *[DZ 139 Tàishàng dòngzhēn níngshén xiūxíng jīngjué](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0139)* preserves a reduced version with significant variants. The poem's vocabulary and imagery are based on the *Wùzhēn piān* 悟真篇 [KR5a0268](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0268), with a style resembling that of Chén Níwán 陳泥丸 (cf. *[Cuìxū piān](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d1090)*); its underlying ideas show marked influence of Chán 禪 Buddhism. The poem polemically rejects many of the popular *nèidān* techniques described in other texts attributed to Zhōnglí Quán and Lǚ Dòngbīn, suggesting that its actual author was affiliated with the *Wùzhēn piān* school. The alchemical process described is accomplished spontaneously upon the discovery and circulation of the *xiāntiān zhī qì* 先天之氣 ("the *qì* of Former Heaven").

**Abstract**

Farzeen Baldrian-Hussein, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 2:832–833 (§3.A.4, *Nèidān* and *Yǎngshēng*), dates the poem to the mid-eleventh century on the strength of (i) its modelling on a *Zhōnglí*-attributed poem that was very much in vogue during the twelfth century, but which it polemically critiques (cf. 1a and *[Wùzhēn piān, Xiūzhēn shíshū](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0268)* 28.5b); (ii) its dependence on *Wùzhēn piān* (1075) terminology; (iii) the absence of pre-Northern-Sòng quotation in its present form; (iv) its polemic against rival Zhōng-Lǚ-attributed *nèidān* programmes, locating it within the Sòng-period sectarian rivalry of the Southern lineage. The pseudepigraphic attribution to Zhōnglí Quán places it within the broader Zhōng Lǚ apocryphal corpus; cf. *[DZ 246 Xīshān qúnxiān huìzhēn jì](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0247)* and *[DZ 263c Zhōng Lǚ chuándào jí](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0266)*. Frontmatter brackets composition broadly in mid-Northern-Sòng, post-*Wùzhēn piān*.
